title: When God Demands Accuracy Over Speed
paragraphs: When God Demands Accuracy Over Speed
Some of you are moving fast, but you are not moving faithfully.

You are rushing to post, rushing to preach, rushing to decide, rushing to answer, rushing to build, rushing to prove that God is using you. But somewhere in the speed, you stopped trembling at the weight of being accurate before God.
And God saw it.
You knew something was off. You felt the check in your spirit. You heard the quiet warning. But the deadline was loud. The opportunity was open. The applause was close. So you moved anyway.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God is not impressed by speed when obedience is missing.
Saul moved quickly when he offered the sacrifice before Samuel arrived. It looked urgent. It looked practical. It even looked spiritual. But God called it disobedience.
Samuel told him, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the Lord your God” (1 Samuel 13:13).
Read that again.
He did something religious, but he did it inaccurately.
That is terrifying.

Because sometimes the danger is not that you are doing the wrong thing. Sometimes the danger is that you are doing the right-looking thing in the wrong spirit, at the wrong time, without God’s permission.
Speed can hide pride.
Accuracy exposes surrender.

Moses struck the rock when God told him to speak to it. Water still came out. The people still drank. The miracle still happened. But Moses was disciplined because he misrepresented God before the people.
The Lord said, “Because you did not believe in me, to uphold me as holy in the eyes of the people of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land” (Numbers 20:12).
That should make every servant of God slow down.
Because results do not always mean approval.

A crowd can grow while accuracy dies. A ministry can expand while holiness is being neglected. A message can go viral while Scripture is being mishandled. A decision can look successful while heaven is calling it compromise.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is not a call to laziness. It is a call to holy precision.
The Bible does not honor careless speed. It says, “Be not rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be hasty to utter a word before God” (Ecclesiastes 5:2).
That means God cares about what you say in His name.
Not just how emotional it sounds.
Not just how many people respond.
Not just how fast you deliver it.
Accuracy matters because God’s name is attached to His Word.
James warned, “Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, for you know that we who teach will be judged with greater strictness” (James 3:1).
That verse should make every preacher, writer, singer, discipler, and content creator tremble.
Because when you speak for God, you are not handling opinions. You are handling souls.
And souls do not need your rushed inspiration.
They need truth.
They need Christ.
They need the Gospel clearly: mankind is sinful, God is holy, judgment is real, Jesus Christ died for sinners, rose again, and commands all people everywhere to repent and believe.
“Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners” (1 Timothy 1:15).
Not entertain sinners.
Not flatter sinners.
Not help sinners feel spiritual while remaining unrepentant.
Save sinners.
That means accuracy is not optional. It is love.
When you rush truth, you may comfort what God is trying to confront. You may soften what God is trying to expose. You may promise peace where God is calling for repentance.
Jeremiah rebuked false prophets who said, “Peace, peace,” when there was no peace (Jeremiah 6:14).
And that still happens today.
People want fast encouragement, but not deep correction. They want a quick word, but not a crucified life. They want God’s promises, but not God’s holiness. They want destiny, but not repentance.
You knew.
You knew the message needed more prayer.
You knew the decision needed more discernment.
You knew the Scripture needed to be studied in context.
You knew your motive was mixed.
But speed gave you an excuse.
God is merciful, but He is not careless. Grace does not mean God stops caring about truth. Grace means Jesus saves us from sin, not that He gives us permission to be sloppy with holy things.
“Study to show yourself approved unto God… rightly dividing the word of truth” (2 Timothy 2:15).
Rightly dividing.
Not quickly twisting.
Not emotionally guessing.
Not forcing a verse to fit your agenda.
The enemy loves inaccurate speed because it feels productive while quietly producing confusion. He does not always need you to deny Scripture. Sometimes he only needs you to misapply it.
A little error can wound a soul.
A half-truth can build a false hope.
A rushed word can lead someone away from repentance.
But when God slows you down, it is not rejection. It may be protection.
He is protecting the people who will hear you.
He is protecting the assignment from your ego.
He is protecting your soul from becoming addicted to momentum.
Jesus never rushed in panic. He moved with perfect obedience to the Father. He said, “The Son can do nothing of his own accord, but only what he sees the Father doing” (John 5:19).
That is accuracy.
Not pressure.
Not performance.
Not proving.
Just surrender.
So slow down long enough to obey.
Pray before you speak. Study before you teach. Repent before you lead. Listen before you move. Let God correct the parts of you that want visibility more than purity.
Because one day, the question will not be, “How fast did you build?”
It will be, “Were you faithful?”
And the only safe place to stand is in Jesus Christ.
Not your gift.
Not your urgency.
Not your platform.
Christ alone.
Comment, “Lord, make me accurate.”
